Sharif Ibrahim Memon vs State Of Maharashtra on 24 November,
2025

Author: Madhav J. Jamdar
Bench: Madhav J. Jamdar

In The High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
 Criminal Appellate Jurisdiction
 Anticipatory Bail Application No.2471 Of 2023
 Shariff Ibrahim Memon & Anr.

entities.text: High Court Of Judicature At Bombay
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
... Applican
 Versus
 The State of Maharashtra ...

Responde
 Mr. Tushar Sonawane, for the Applicants.
Ms. R.V. Newton, App, for the Respondent-State.

Mr. Bhushan Sanju Chavan, Killa Police Station, Malegaon,
 present.

Coram: Madhav J. Jamdar, J.
 Dated : 24th November 2025

Pc:- 
 1. Heard Mr. Sonawane, learned Counsel appearing for the  Applicants and Ms. Newton, learned APP appearing for the  Respondent-State.
 2. By this Application, the Applicants are seeking pre-arrest ba  in connection with C.R. No. 140 of 2023 registered on 22 nd July  2023 under Sections 328, 188, 272, 273 read with Section 34 of Sharif Ibrahim Memon vs State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52354933/
1  the Indian Penal Code, 1860 ("IPC") with Killa Police Station,
 District - Nashik (Rural).
 Page 1  ::: Uploaded on - 25/11/2025 ::: Downloaded on - 2  603-ABA-2471-2023.DOC  Akash Tayde  3.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As per the prosecution case the Applicants were found  dealing with contraband material which is unsafe and dangerous  for the health of people.
4. It is the submission of Mr. Sonawane, learned Counsel that  except the offence under Section 328 of IPC, all other offences are  bailable offences.
He submits that as far as Section 328 of IPC is  concerned, the Supreme Court is considering the applicability of Section 328 of IPC to the similar cases.
He therefore, states that  the Anticipatory Bail be granted.
5. On the other hand, Ms. Newton, learned APP strongly  opposes the Anticipatory Bail Application.
She submits that the  offence is very serious and therefore, the Anticipatory Bail  Application be rejected.

Learned APP submits that there is one  antecedent being C.R. No.260 of 2015 for the offences punishable  under Sections 188, 272, 273, 328 and 26(2)(i), 3(i)(zz)(v), 26(2)
 (iv), 27(3)(d) and under Section 27(3)(e) of the Food Safety and Sharif Ibrahim Memon vs State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52354933/
2  Standard Act, 2006.

entities.text: Food Safety and Sharif Ibrahim Memon vs State Of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Akash Tayde  6.

Learned APP submits that if this Court is inclined to grant  Anticipatory Bail then the Applicants be directed to give  undertaking in terms of order of the Supreme Court in the case of  Abhijit Jitendra Lolage vs State of Maharashtra 1 and more  particularly relies on following condition imposed by the Supreme  Court in case of similar offences :-
 "It is deemed appropriate to impose the  condition - "I, Abhijeet Jitendra Lolage do  undertake to not deal with Gutkha, that is, Pan  Masala with Tobacco".

entities.text: Abhijit Jitendra Lolage vs State of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In case, the appellant -  Abhijeet Jitendra Lolage violates the terms and  conditions of bail, including the undertaking  imposed, it would be open to the prosecution to  seek cancellation of bail ".
(Emphasis added)

Mr. Sonawane, learned Counsel appearing for all the Applicants,
 after taking the instructions submits that the Applicant will give  the undertaking.

7. The Supreme Court in the said order has imposed the above Sharif Ibrahim Memon vs State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52354933/
3  condition in case of similar offence.

Akash Tayde  8.
Perusal of the record shows that except the offence under Section 328 of IPC the other offences are bailable offences.
The  issue whether Section 328 of IPC will apply to similar cases is  pending before the Supreme Court.

Although there is one  antecedent a learned Single Judge by order dated 19 th November  2015 passed in Criminal Anticipatory Bail Application No.1586 of  2015 has granted Anticipatory Bail and the said offence is of the  year 2015.

entities.text: Criminal Anticipatory Bail Application No.1586 of  2015
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text: As the Applicants are ready to give the undertaking that  they will not deal with Gutkha and Tobacco products in any  manner whatsoever, the case is made out for grant of Anticipatory  Bail.
All the Applicants have been protected by Learned Single  Judge (N.J. Jamadar J.) by order dated 7th September 2023.

9 . In view thereof, the following order is passed:
 ORDER (a) In the event of arrest of the Applicant No.1-. Shariff Ibrahim Memon and Applicant No.2- Mohammad Yusuf Mohammad Ashraf in connection with C.R. No.140 of 2023 registered with the Sharif Ibrahim Memon vs State Of Maharashtra on 24 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/52354933/
4

entities.text: Sharif Ibrahim Memon vs State Of Maharashtra
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Killa Police Station, District Nashik (Rural) the Applicants are directed to be released on bail on their furnishing P.R. Page 4 603-ABA-2471-2023.DOC Akash Tayde Bond in the sum of Rs.1,00,000/- each with one or two solvent sureties in the like amount.
(b) The Applicants shall attend the concerned Police Station once in a month till filing of the chargesheet and shall cooperate with the investigation.

(c) The Applicants to furnish undertakings that they will not deal with banned products i.e. Gutkha,
Pan Masala with Tobacco products in any manner whatsoever.
Such undertakings are to be filed in this Court within a period of two weeks from today.
The Applicants to strictly comply with the said undertaking.
(d) The Applicants shall furnish their cell phone numbers and residential addresses to the Investigating Officer and shall keep the same updated, in case of any change thereto.

(e) The Applicants shall not directly or indirectly make any inducement, threat, or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade such a person from disclosing the facts to the Court or Page 5 603-ABA-2471-2023.DOC Akash Tayde to any Police personnel.
(f) The Applicants shall not tamper with the prosecution evidence and shall not contact or influence the Complainant or any witness in any manner.
(g) The Applicants shall not leave India without prior permission of the Court.
(h) In case, the Applicant violates the terms and conditions of bail, including the undertaking, it would be open to the prosecution to seek cancellation of bail.
10. The Anticipatory Bail Application is disposed of accordingly.
